items.definition: The process of learning knowledge and skills, usually at school.
items.sentence: Our teacher says a good education helps you follow any dream.
items.hint: The 'shun' ending on this word is spelt -tion, the most common choice.

items.definition: Harmful rubbish or dirt that damages the air, land or water.
items.sentence: Picking up litter at the beach helps stop pollution spreading into the sea.
items.hint: Double l in the middle, then the -tion ending for the 'shun' sound.

items.definition: A note or message asking someone to come to an event.
items.sentence: Every classmate received an invitation to the end of term party.
items.hint: Invite drops its final e before adding -ation.

items.definition: Something pretty you add to make a place or object look special.
items.sentence: Dad let me choose one shiny decoration for the top of the tree.
items.hint: Start with decorate, drop the final e, then add -ion.

items.definition: The number of people or animals living in a place.
items.sentence: Our town's population grows every summer when visitors arrive for the surf.
items.hint: It ends in -ation: populate drops the e and adds -ion.

items.definition: A step that tells you exactly what to do.
items.sentence: Nathan read each instruction carefully before building his model rocket.
items.hint: Build it from instruct plus -ion, so the ending is -tion.

items.definition: Taking one number away from another in maths.
items.sentence: Maya checked her subtraction twice before handing in the maths test.
items.hint: Take subtract and simply add -ion to the end.

items.definition: Something that keeps you safe from harm.
items.sentence: Sunscreen and a hat give great protection on a hot summer day.
items.hint: Protect plus -ion gives the -tion ending.

items.definition: What you do or feel straight after something happens.
items.sentence: The goalkeeper's quick reaction saved the final penalty of the match.
items.hint: React plus -ion; the ending is -tion, never -shun.

items.definition: A very large and grand house.
items.sentence: The old mansion on the hill has twenty rooms and a huge garden.
items.hint: This 'shun' sound is spelt -sion after the n.

items.definition: An extra part added to make something longer or bigger.
items.sentence: Our school's new extension has beanbags and shelves of graphic novels.
items.hint: Extend changes its d to s, so the ending is -sion, not -tion.

items.definition: The slow wearing away of land by wind or water.
items.sentence: Rangers planted grasses along the dunes to slow the erosion nearby.
items.hint: After a vowel the 'zhun' sound is spelt -sion, as in erode becoming this word.

items.definition: An important job or task someone is sent to do.
items.sentence: Their mission today is to find ten spiral shells along the shore.
items.hint: Double s then -ion: the -ssion ending makes the 'shun' sound.

items.definition: Being let into a place, or the price you pay to get in.
items.sentence: The zoo offers free admission for kids during the school holidays.
items.hint: Admit swaps its t for a double s before -ion.

items.definition: A show where people play music for a crowd.
items.sentence: Tickets for the spring concert sold out in less than an hour.
items.hint: The c before e is soft and sounds like s.

items.definition: A grand building where a king or queen lives.
items.sentence: We built a sand palace with four towers and a deep moat.
items.hint: The final ce is a soft c that sounds like s.

items.definition: To see or become aware of something; also a written sign.
items.sentence: Did you notice the new mural painted on the gym wall?
items.hint: Say no-tiss but write the soft ending -ice.

items.definition: Happening a short time ago.
items.sentence: Her most recent drawing shows a lorikeet perched on our back fence.
items.hint: The c sounds like s because it comes before e.

items.definition: Fruit like oranges, lemons and limes with juicy segments and zesty skin.
items.sentence: Our citrus trees drop juicy lemons over the back fence all winter.
items.hint: The c before i is soft, so it sounds like s.

items.definition: A person who belongs to a country or town.
items.sentence: Grandpa became an Australian citizen at a joyful town hall event last year.
items.hint: The c is soft before i, so it sounds like s.

items.definition: A powerful spinning storm with strong winds and heavy rain.
items.sentence: News reports said the cyclone would curve away before reaching the coast.
items.hint: The first c is soft before y and sounds like s.

items.definition: A room where people work at desks.
items.sentence: Please take this note to the front office before the bell rings.
items.hint: Double f in the middle and a soft ce at the end.

items.definition: Minced pork or beef shaped into a long thin roll for grilling.
items.sentence: Dad flipped each sausage carefully so nothing burnt on the grill.
items.hint: The ending -age uses a soft g that sounds like j.

items.definition: A small, cosy house, often in the countryside.
items.sentence: We stayed in a stone cottage near the river during the holidays.
items.hint: Double t, then the soft g ending -age.

items.definition: The bags and suitcases you pack for a trip.
items.sentence: The porter stacked our luggage onto a trolley at the airport.
items.hint: Double g in the middle, then the soft g in -age.

items.definition: A plump grey bird that coos and struts around parks.
items.sentence: One cheeky pigeon strutted over our picnic rug hunting for crusts.
items.hint: The e after the g keeps it soft, sounding like j.

items.definition: A gas in the air that living things need to breathe.
items.sentence: Divers carry tanks of oxygen so they can explore underwater reefs.
items.hint: The g before e is soft: oxy plus gen.

items.definition: Easily broken or damaged, so it must be handled with care.
items.sentence: The label warned that the fragile parcel held Grandma's glass vase.
items.hint: Soft g before i, and it ends in -ile.

items.definition: To rest your weight on your knees.
items.sentence: The gardener had to kneel on a soft pad while planting seedlings.
items.hint: Silent k at the start, then a double e.

items.definition: One of the bony joints where your fingers bend.
items.sentence: Ben scraped a knuckle while climbing over the old wooden fence.
items.hint: Start with a silent k before the n, and end with -le.

items.definition: A fastening made by twisting and tying rope or string.
items.sentence: At camp we learnt to tie a reef knot in under a minute.
items.hint: The rope word begins with a silent k.

items.definition: A small imaginary person, often shown as a garden statue with a pointy hat.
items.sentence: A chubby garden gnome with a red hat stands beside our letterbox.
items.hint: A silent g sits before the n at the start.

items.definition: A tiny piece of bread or cake.
items.sentence: Not a single crumb was left after Nan sliced her banana bread.
items.hint: It ends with a silent b, like thumb and lamb.

items.definition: A tradesperson who fixes water pipes and taps.
items.sentence: The plumber turned up before lunch and fixed our dripping kitchen tap.
items.hint: The silent b from plumb stays in place before -er.

items.definition: A soft white stick used for writing on boards or paths.
items.sentence: Ivy drew a hopscotch grid with chalk on the concrete path.
items.hint: The l is silent, like in walk and talk.

items.definition: To close or join something firmly, like a seatbelt or button.
items.sentence: Please fasten your seatbelt before the bus pulls out of the carpark.
items.hint: The t is silent: say fas-en but keep the t.

items.definition: A large pink-fleshed fish that swims in rivers and the ocean.
items.sentence: Dad grilled some salmon with lemon for our dinner on Friday night.
items.hint: The l is silent: say sam-on but write the l.

items.definition: The yellow middle part of an egg.
items.sentence: The golden yolk spilled over the pan edge when the egg cracked.
items.hint: The l is silent, just like in folk.

items.definition: A piece of furniture with doors and shelves for storing things.
items.sentence: The snacks live in the highest cupboard where little hands cannot reach.
items.hint: It is cup plus board, but the p goes silent when you say it.

items.definition: A small crease or fold in skin, cloth or paper.
items.sentence: Mum smoothed every wrinkle out of the picnic blanket before lunch.
items.hint: It starts with a silent w before the r, like write.

items.definition: The person in charge of a school.
items.sentence: Our principal revealed there will be a pyjama day next Friday.
items.hint: The school leader is your pal, so this one ends in -pal.

items.definition: An outdoor fair with stalls, games and treats, often run by a school.
items.sentence: Our school fete raised money for new shade sails this year.
items.hint: The fair is f-e-t-e; fate with an a means destiny.

items.definition: To do something over and over so you get better at it.
items.sentence: The team meets every Tuesday to practise passing and shooting goals.
items.hint: In Australian English the verb takes -ise, just like advise.

items.definition: The sweet food served at the end of a meal.
items.sentence: For dessert we shared warm apple pie with a scoop of ice cream.
items.hint: Double s because you always want a second serving of the sweet one.

items.definition: The part of a bike or car that slows it down.
items.sentence: Squeeze the back brake softly as you roll down the steep driveway.
items.hint: Use -ake for the stopping part; the other spelling means to smash.

items.definition: To dig a hole and cover something with earth.
items.sentence: Our puppy loves to bury his chew toys beside the lemon tree.
items.hint: It starts like burrow with bur, even though it rhymes with berry.

items.definition: A small dried grape used in baking.
items.sentence: Nan added a plump currant to the top of every little bun.
items.hint: The dried fruit ends in -ant; electric flow ends in -ent.

items.definition: Rough and grainy, not smooth or fine.
items.sentence: The coarse sand near the dunes felt scratchy under our feet.
items.hint: Rough sand contains oar, like the rough wooden oar of a boat.

items.definition: To fly high in the sky without flapping.
items.sentence: We watched a sea eagle soar above the cliffs all morning.
items.hint: To fly high has oar in it; the -ore spelling means painful.

items.definition: To get better again after an injury.
items.sentence: The vet said the kitten's paw would heal within a fortnight.
items.hint: It has ea like health; the -eel spelling is part of your foot.

items.definition: The narrow middle part of your body above your hips.
items.sentence: Tie the sash around your waist before the costume parade begins.
items.hint: Your middle has ai in it; the other spelling means rubbish.

items.definition: A person invited to visit or stay.
items.sentence: Every guest at the party signed a card for Grandad's birthday.
items.hint: A visitor starts with gu-, like guess without the past tense ending.

items.definition: The long hair on the neck of a horse or lion.
items.sentence: Ella brushed the pony's tangled mane until it shone like silk.
items.hint: Hair on a horse ends in -ane; the -ain spelling means most important.

items.definition: The daily rise and fall of the sea on the shore.
items.sentence: At low tide we found tiny crabs hiding among the rocks.
items.hint: The sea's rise has i-consonant-e; the other spelling comes from tie.

items.definition: A small natural waterway you can splash across.
items.sentence: We cooled our feet in the shallow creek behind the campsite.
items.hint: The waterway has double e; the ea spelling is a squeaky sound.

items.definition: Not covered by anything; plain or empty.
items.sentence: Leo tiptoed over the hot driveway in bare feet after his swim.
items.hint: Uncovered is b-a-r-e; the -ear spelling is the big furry animal.

items.definition: Having a rough, croaky voice, often after shouting.
items.sentence: Milly sounded hoarse after cheering so loudly at the relay races.
items.hint: The croaky voice hides oars inside; the animal spelling has none.

items.definition: A shellfish with a dark hinged shell that clings to rocks.
items.sentence: Tom found a glossy mussel shell washed up near the jetty.
items.hint: The shellfish has double s and ends in -el, not -le.

items.definition: The part someone plays in a show, team or job.
items.sentence: Priya scored the lead role in this year's school musical.
items.hint: A part in a play is r-o-l-e; the -oll spelling is bread or a tumble.

items.definition: A pleasant smell, like perfume or flowers.
items.sentence: The lovely scent of jasmine drifted through the open classroom window.
items.hint: A smell starts with sc- and a silent c, like science.

items.definition: A green vegetable with tightly packed flower heads.
items.sentence: Steamed broccoli tastes much better with a little melted cheese on top.
items.hint: Remember double c but only one l near the end.

items.definition: A small flat baked treat that snaps when you bite it.
items.sentence: Jack dunked his biscuit in warm milk until it went soft.
items.hint: After bis- comes -cuit; the u hides quietly after the c.

items.definition: A shop that sells medicines, or the person who prepares them.
items.sentence: Mum ducked into the chemist to buy sunscreen and a hairbrush.
items.hint: It starts with ch- that sounds like k, just like chemistry.

items.definition: A sour liquid used to flavour chips and salads.
items.sentence: Salt and vinegar chips are the first to vanish at every sleepover.
items.hint: It ends in -ar, not -er: there is a sour ar at the end.

items.definition: A leafy green salad plant.
items.sentence: Crisp lettuce leaves make the perfect base for our garden salad.
items.hint: Double t in the middle and the surprise ending -uce.

items.definition: An outdoor grill for cooking food, or a party where you use one.
items.sentence: Everyone brought a salad to share at our street barbecue yesterday.
items.hint: It ends in -cue: bar-be-cue, three little parts in one word.

items.definition: Very bright or extremely clever.
items.sentence: Everyone agreed the fireworks finale was absolutely brilliant this year.
items.hint: Double l in the middle: bril-li-ant.

items.definition: A pear-shaped green fruit with creamy flesh and a large seed.
items.sentence: Nina sliced a creamy avocado on top of her spicy nachos.
items.hint: It starts with avo-, not ava-: a-v-o-c-a-d-o.

items.definition: Really and honestly; in a way that is completely real.
items.sentence: Camping under the stars felt truly magical on our last night.
items.hint: True drops its e before adding -ly.

items.definition: The number that comes straight after thirty-nine.
items.sentence: Nearly forty students signed up for the beach clean-up this term.
items.hint: Four loses its u when it becomes this bigger number.

items.definition: A word meaning even though, used to join two ideas.
items.sentence: We kept playing cricket although a few drops of rain fell.
items.hint: It is all plus though, but with only one l.

items.definition: From one side to the other.
items.sentence: Mia swam across the rock pool without stopping once.
items.hint: Just one c: it is simply a plus cross.

items.definition: A musical instrument with six strings you strum or pluck.
items.sentence: Ollie strummed his guitar softly while we sang after dinner.
items.hint: It starts with gu- like guest: g-u-i-t-a-r.

items.definition: A gathering of the whole school to share news and awards.
items.sentence: Our class performed a bush dance at assembly on Friday morning.
items.hint: Double s near the start: as-sem-bly.

items.definition: A fun event with races, games or rides.
items.sentence: Our house won the spirit award at the athletics carnival today.
items.hint: It ends in -val with a single l: car-ni-val.

items.definition: Feeling upset because someone has something you want.
items.sentence: Ruby felt jealous when her brother scored the window seat again.
items.hint: There is a hidden ea after the j, and it ends in -ous.

items.definition: Very bad or unpleasant.
items.sentence: The milk smelt awful after it sat out in the sun.
items.hint: Awe drops its e, then add -ful with one l.

items.definition: A flying machine with wings and engines.
items.sentence: The little aeroplane wobbled slightly as it landed on the grassy strip.
items.hint: Australian English starts it with aero-, like aerobics.

items.definition: To fail to win, or to be unable to find something.
items.sentence: Nobody wants to lose the trophy after training so hard all season.
items.hint: One o only: the double o spelling means not tight.

items.definition: The particular taste of a food or drink.
items.sentence: Mango is easily the best milkshake flavour on the whole menu.
items.hint: Australian English ends it with -our, like colour and neighbour.
